links.outcome: Readability of chatbot patient counseling text versus NIH sixth-grade recommendation
links.effect: All chatbots exceeded the sixth-grade level; mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.3 (platform means 11.4-13.7); no platform met readability benchmarks.
links.quote: All chatbots produced text far exceeding the NIH-recommended sixth-grade level (mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.3; platform means 11.4-13.7) (Fig. 4).

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education text
links.effect: Flesch Reading Ease 26.4 (ChatGPT) to 42.1 (DeepSeek); mean FKGL 12.3; no platform met recommended readability benchmarks.
links.quote: No platform met recommended readability benchmarks.

links.outcome: Proportion of chatbot responses citing sources or indicating information currency
links.effect: Only 27.5% of responses cited sources; 5.0% indicated information currency.
links.quote: Transparency was uniformly deficient: only 27.5% of responses cited sources, and a mere 5.0% indicated information currency (Fig. 3).

screen.reason: Evaluates off-the-shelf LLM chatbot responses to patient questions on robot-assisted colorectal surgery for quality, readability, and transparency, but does not test or compare specific deployment safeguards or practices.
